uncited: Initialize all output samples $A_i = 0$ for all $i$.
Identify all input samples $X_j$ that lie within the support of the kernel centered at $I$.
Calculate the relative distance $u = I - X_j$ (or appropriate coordinate transformation).
Update the output sample: $A_i \leftarrow A_i + X_j \cdot w$.
Return the array of output samples $A_i$.
- $A_i$ is the value of the $i$-th output sample.
- $X_j$ is the value of the $j$-th input sample.
- $\text{support}(I)$ is the set of input indices $j$ such that $K(I - X_j) \neq 0$.
- Kernel support: Determines the number of input samples accessed per output sample.
- **Kernel Support Boundaries:** Ensure that the loop over input samples correctly handles cases where the kernel support extends beyond the input data boundaries.
- Time Complexity: $O(N_{out} \cdot N_{kernel})$, where $N_{out}$ is the number of output samples and $N_{kernel}$ is the number of input samples within the kernel support for each output.
- Memory Complexity: $O(N_{in} + N_{out})$ for storing input and output samples.
It is a fundamental technique in volume rendering for resampling and reconstructing volume data onto a screen-space grid.
